newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Irkutskenergo plans ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Irkutskenergo plans ADR issue.

text.p: Russian power utility Irkutskenergo is planning an issue of level one American Depositary Receipts later this year, advisers to the firm said on Tuesday.
A date for the issue, which would not be in the form of a private placement, has not yet been set, a director of investment group Brunswick told Reuters.
The Bank of New York will act as depositary bank for the issue.

"Irkutskenergo have indicated their interest in establishing a level one ADR programme with the Bank of New York," Chris Sturdy, the bank's vice-president for depositary receipts programmes, told Reuters.
"I would say it was some weeks off before they get the requisite exemptions from the SEC and complete the documentation requirements," he added.
Irkutskoye AO Energetiki i Elektrifikatsii is 40 percent state-owned. The remaining 60 percent is divided roughly equally between Russian and foreign investors, Brunswick said.
Irkutskenergo has generation capacity of 12,914 MW and is Russia's biggest generator, according to a research report issued earlier this year by MC Securities.
It is one of just two "energos", as the Russian regional generators are known, in which the Unified Energy System national grid company does not hold a stake.
Irkutskenergo shares are among the most liquid on the Russian Trading System. They stood at 10.9 cents each at 1220 GMT, down from 11 cents at Monday's close.
ADRs are securities which allow overseas investors access to foreign shares without the complexities of settlement in the issuer's market.
Level one ADRs, which have been issued by a number of Russian companies already, are the simplest and do not raise new capital.
